narrative:
The model determined that you have a 55% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The loan amount of 4006 DM also worked against you. Approved applicants request an average of about 3020 DM, so your larger request increased the perceived risk and added further weight toward denial.

Your purpose—financing a new car—provided the third-largest influence. While many people finance cars, this reason pulled the prediction slightly toward higher risk compared with more common purposes such as radio or furniture.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed the rest of your profile and led to the denial.

What you should do next is improve your checking-account balance and, if possible, reduce the amount you need to borrow. Once your account shows a positive or zero balance and you can request a smaller sum, your risk profile will look considerably stronger and you can reapply with a much better chance of approval.
